source.title: Embedding Principle: a hierarchical structure of loss landscape of deep neural networks
source.authors: Yaoyu Zhang; Yuqing Li; Zhongwang Zhang; Tao Luo; Z. Xu

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. It includes a figure whose plotted values are not transcribed numerically; the accompanying text describes the relevant result.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves theoretical relations between critical points of networks of different widths and discusses generalization, but does not test held-out error or any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on generalization and flat minima, but those cited results are not its own. Its Figure 3 experiment reports training loss and fitted functions, not test error or a training-to-test gap.
record.test_reason: The study proves relations between critical points of networks of different widths. Its Figure 3 experiment reports training loss and fitted functions, without held-out performance. Neither these results nor its conjectures test V1–V8; width-dependent optimization geometry does not establish V2, and Hessian properties without generalization gaps do not test V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors prove output- and criticality-preserving embeddings from narrower into wider networks, analyze embedded critical submanifolds and transitions to strict saddles, and conjecture an implicit training bias toward simple critical functions. Their generalization implications remain conjectural.

fits_no_version.finding: In Figure 3, a width-500 two-layer tanh network fitting 50 points first approaches the best width-1 fit, then approaches the best width-3 fit that interpolates the training points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A wide tanh network can pass through functions resembling narrower-network fits as its learned function becomes more complex during training.

record.problems: The generalization implications are conjectural in this paper. The Figure 3 experiment describes training loss and fitted outputs but reports no held-out evaluation or uncertainty.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and held-out accuracy under natural versus random labels.
Test error as trained network width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Generalization comparisons between convolutional and fully connected image classifiers.
Held-out performance of adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning regimes.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted recipes.
Dropout effects on held-out error and interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness correlations with training–test gaps and comparisons with other generalization measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing highly memorized versus randomly selected training examples.

record.verdict_notes: Section 4.3 describes the interpolation as avoiding overfitting, but supplies no held-out evaluation or quantitative generalization comparison. This characterization does not warrant a verdict on any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out performance on natural and random labels.
Test error across widths beyond the interpolation threshold for the specified ReLU networks and datasets.
Convolutional versus fully connected image-classification generalization.
Held-out performance comparisons among adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers.
Held-out performance under varied batch sizes and training recipes.
Held-out error effects of dropout and its interaction with dataset size, augmentation, and weight decay.
Whether magnitude-aware sharpness tracks the train-test gap.
Whether removing memorized examples changes held-out accuracy.

rows.subject: two-layer tanh neural network with 500 hidden neurons
rows.operation_detail: Fit 50 data points; authors describe the output function at selected stages of training.
rows.measure: Training loss and output-function fit progression
rows.value: At the first stage, the output is close to the best fitting of the width-1 tanh NN; at the second, it is close to the width-3 tanh NN and interpolates all data points.
rows.note: The text describes the plotted training loss and selected output functions; it gives no test-error measure.
rows.check: The reported training progression is accurate, but cannot establish any claim version. Figure 3 compares the width-500 network's outputs with global-minimum fits of width-1 and width-3 networks; these comparators should replace the unspecified baseline. No held-out error is reported.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
